learn.title: Stop Giving Your Agent Tools. Give It a Sandbox - Mikyo King, Arize AI
learn.headline: Let agents write code in a sandbox instead of calling many tools
learn.reason: Arize reports 43% fewer tokens; a cheaper agent-loop design you can try.

card.headline: Talk: let AI helpers write code, not take steps one by one
card.gist: An AI that takes actions, called an agent, usually does them one at a time. A talk from Arize AI says: let it write a small program instead.
card.picture: Picture exporting every table to a spreadsheet and reading all the rows to find one number. Writing one SQL query that joins and filters is much simpler. Only the answer comes back, not every raw row.
card.why_you: When you build an agent, you may give it a long list of actions. This talk offers a different design to test, and it also names that design's costs.
card.remember: Let the agent write code, and bring back only what's needed.
card.term_meaning: The agent writes code in a sandbox to combine tools and return only needed results.
card.say_it: I'd let the agent combine tools in sandboxed code, so raw outputs stay out of context.
card.follow_up_why: Tool lists and raw outputs fill the context and cost tokens; code returns only answers.
card.reality_check: This is Arize's own talk, not an independent test. Its Harbor evals showed 43% fewer tokens, 31% lower cost. The video is on YouTube.
card.try_it: Watch the hidden-costs chapter at 8:19 and write down the four risks it names.
